correctness.rationale: For the eighth Stirling column, exact inclusion-exclusion bounds the valuation of the even-base approximation error by \(n-5\) once \(n\ge8\). The parity-branch Mahler series have odd linear coefficients 17 and 21, and every nonlinear coefficient satisfies a strict 2-adic divided-difference bound. Consequently the even branch and the normalized odd branch are isometries of \(\mathbb Z_2\), hence each permutes classes modulo \(2^k\). The odd branch has an additional factor four. This proves the complete residue fibers, with \(k=1\) handled separately, and the least eventual period. The standalone checker verifies finite instances but is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: For each modulus \(2^k\) and target residue \(y\), the theorem solves the natural congruence \(S(n,8)\equiv y\pmod{2^k}\) and supplies its exact multiplicity in an eventual period. The eighth Stirling column counts partitions into eight blocks. The explicit two-isometry decomposition exhibits a striking nonuniform arithmetic output law and determines a natural 2-adic distribution not obtainable merely from the previously established periods or valuations.
